answer: The satisfies operator, added in TypeScript 4.9, validates that an expression matches a type without widening the inferred type.

results.title: TypeScript: Documentation - TypeScript 4.9
results.content: TypeScript 4.9 introduces the new satisfies operator, which lets us validate that the type of an expression matches some type, without changing the resulting type of that expression.

results.title: Clarifying the `satisfies` Operator | Total TypeScript
results.content: The satisfies operator is a way to tell TypeScript that a value conforms to a type, while still letting TypeScript infer the most specific type.

results.title: satisfies vs as in TypeScript
results.content: Unlike a type assertion with as, satisfies never silences an error.
